reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a rummy and betting app with an unusually easy-income claim of earning 400 to 500 rupees daily from a ten-rupee investment, while instructing viewers to create an account, add money, play prediction games and use referral features. The video presents the app and its gameplay, bonuses and payment screens as a practical earning method, encouraging participation rather than warning about the offer.

citations.quote: Earn Daliy 500₹-1000₹
you are going to get 400 to 500 rupees of daily money in a ten-rupee investment
you get the commission after you click on any monkey game you'll join
If you lose a single bat, you'll have to add an Admin. So I want you to add 50 rupees.

opening.argument: Judge, the warning deserves weight alongside the earning headline. The speaker says the app is dangerous and tells viewers not to use it. The description also states an educational purpose and disclaims support for illegal activity. Those statements do not erase the money claims, but they make it harder to treat the video as an unqualified assurance that viewers should expect an easy return. The stronger reading is that the creator is showing a risky offer while cautioning viewers about it.

citations.quote: But don't do this app is really dangerous
This channel has been not supported illegal activity this video has been only educational purpose
Earn Daliy 500₹-1000₹

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution quotes a daily-income claim and an instruction to add money, but those excerpts do not establish that the speaker presents participation as risk-free. The same transcript contains an express danger warning. Even the cited instruction follows a stated loss condition, which matters when deciding whether the video is concealing risk or discussing it.

citations.quote: But don't do this app is really dangerous
If you lose a single bat, you'll have to add an Admin. So I want you to add 50 rupees.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The isolated warning does not define the video's overall message. The title promises daily earnings, the speaker describes daily money from a ten-rupee investment, and later asks viewers to add money. An educational-purpose disclaimer does not turn those concrete earning and participation prompts into a warning.

citations.quote: Earn Daliy 500₹-1000₹
you are going to get 400 to 500 rupees of daily money in a ten-rupee investment
So I want you to add 50 rupees.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the spoken material is a walk-through of what appears on the app and how the game proceeds. The speaker introduces the app, describes creating an ID, and asks viewers to focus on gameplay and think for themselves. The sampled screens show an app lobby and a betting board. That supports reading the video as an operational demonstration, even though its title uses an earnings pitch. Showing where a bonus or game feature appears is not, by itself, proof that the claimed daily income was achieved or that every viewer will achieve it.

citations.quote: Now we'll tell you about this app. You have to create it. Okay, just like you have to create an ID in it
I have to focus on the gameplay. So if you guys don't understand a little bit, you have to think for yourself.
Earn Daliy 500₹-1000₹

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats account creation, game screens and bonuses as proof of solicitation. They also fit a walk-through: the speaker explicitly says to focus on gameplay, and the sampled board displays play in progress. Neither the quoted commission line nor the sampled board establishes that a viewer received the advertised daily earnings.

citations.quote: I have to focus on the gameplay.
you get the commission after you click on any monkey game you'll join

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstration is part of the pitch, not separate from it. The speaker ties watching the video to learning how to get daily money from a small investment, then discusses account creation and adding funds. Whether the advertised return is visibly fulfilled is not the issue: the video presents gameplay as a way to earn it.

citations.quote: you are going to get 400 to 500 rupees of daily money in a ten-rupee investment. If you watch this video, you will know in full detail
just like you have to create an ID in it
So I want you to add 50 rupees.

opening.argument: Judge, the material also depicts recognizable in-app promotions: a sign-up bonus, a referral commission and a game lobby with payment and withdrawal controls. Those features can be described without assuming the service is safe, or that the video proves anyone earned the headline amount. The prosecution has evidence of an earnings pitch and a request to add money, but the supplied excerpts do not establish a guaranteed payout, a required referral downline or a credential-harvesting step. On this narrower view, the video is promoting app rewards and gameplay, while the mechanism needed to infer a deceptive scheme remains unproven.

citations.quote: This is how you get a sign bonus of this money.
you get the commission after you click on any monkey game you'll join
So I want you to add 50 rupees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's deposit and commission quotes show participation and a promotional feature; neither, on its own, establishes a fraudulent withdrawal condition or a referral requirement imposed on viewers. The lobby visibly presents games alongside referral, payment and withdrawal controls. That context permits an ordinary app-promotion reading, though it does not verify the earnings claim.

citations.quote: you get the commission after you click on any monkey game you'll join
So I want you to add 50 rupees.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A hidden withdrawal trap or credential request is not necessary to assess the pitch shown here. The title advertises substantial daily earnings, the speaker links daily money to a ten-rupee investment, and the walk-through includes adding funds and earning commissions. The presence of familiar app controls does not substantiate the promised returns or make the easy-income promotion ordinary.
